headline: TechCrunch's podcast hosts call Amazon's decision to drop secrecy agreements in data-centre talks a good first step but doubt it will quickly win over opponents.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the news (Amazon's NDA announcement) is from 2 Oct 2026 and today's piece is podcast commentary.
importance_line: It matters to residents and local officials negotiating over planned data centres, who may now be able to discuss projects openly, then to the companies trying to win over opponents, but this is commentary from TechCrunch's hosts and nothing yet shows that ending NDAs changes opposition.
summary: TechCrunch's Equity podcast discusses the decision, which TechCrunch reported on 3 Oct 2026, by Amazon Web Services, the cloud arm of Amazon, to stop using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs), contracts that bar officials from discussing a project, when negotiating data-centre deals with local governments, following a similar step by Microsoft earlier this year. The hosts, giving their own views, say secret negotiation is at the root of the backlash and the move is a good first step, but that opponents are entrenched and, in one host's view, moratoriums lasting a year or two may have little lasting effect on buildings that will not open for years.
notes: Commentary item; opinions are attributed to the hosts and kept apart from the reported facts. Amazon's announcement date comes from other outlets (About Amazon, WIRED, Data Center Dynamics, 2 Oct 2026) and TechCrunch's 3 Oct article.
